bugs.text: Challenging stage soft-locks on the first hit: challengeWaveAlive is only decremented when an enemy flies off-screen, never when it is destroyed, so once the player kills any enemy in a wave the counter never reaches 0, the next wave never spawns, updateChallenge has no empty-enemies fallback, and the game sits forever on an empty screen (Enter and P do nothing). Reaching stage 3 effectively ends the game.

Challenge bonuses (1,000 per wave, 10,000 PERFECT) are only accumulated into challengeBonus for display and are never added to game.score; and because of the soft-lock they can never be earned anyway.

Enemies in 'waiting' state are created at their formation slot and drawn there (and are shootable) for up to ~2 s at stage start, then jump to the off-screen entry start when their delay expires: the formation appears spawned in place before it flies in.

Entry and return paths end at the static slot position while the formation sways by up to 14 px (5 px once complete) and breathes, so every arriving enemy snaps sideways on the frame it joins the formation.
A rescued captive is not drawn while in 'freed' state, so the fly-down and docking are invisible; the dual fighter just appears ~2 s after the boss is shot.

boss.escorts is never cleared after escorts return to formation; a later solo dive (the 45% no-escort branch or a captive-carrying boss) still counts those old escorts and pays 800/1600 instead of 400.

All 8 enemies of a challenge wave spawn at the same point at the same time with the same base y (challengeBaseY is computed but unused), so they fly as one overlapping clump that only slowly spreads out.

Every enemy fires unaimed bullets from formation and while entering (about 0.3%/enemy/frame, 8 on screen), a constant rain the arcade does not have; the automated play-test lost all three ships in roughly 12 s of play on stage 1 (4-play-015s.png is already back at the title with 1000 points).
startReturning always begins at y=-16, so escorts whose boss is destroyed mid-screen, and the boss and escorts after a return is triggered, teleport to the top of the screen instead of flying there.
Ramming a full-health Boss Galaga only damages it (hp 2 to 1) rather than destroying it, while the player dies.
The title screen draws the HUD reserve ships from the stale game.reserve, so it shows 2 ships before the first game and 0 after a game over.

summary: This is a tidy, well-organised file: a single state object, clear update/render split, Bezier path helpers, pixel-art sprites and a 5x7 font as data, synthesized Web Audio for every required sound, a proper fixed-step loop, and the full tractor-beam / capture / rescue / dual-fighter / hostile-captive chain actually wired up and reachable, which is rare. Stages 1 and 2 feel like Galaga: curved entries, a swaying then breathing formation, boss dives with Goei escorts, a widening striped beam, two-hit colour-changing bosses, READY/GAME OVER/results flow and arcade badge denominations. The fidelity breaks down in the details: every enemy sprays unaimed bullets from the formation so stage 1 is far more lethal than the arcade, enemies are briefly visible parked in their slots before they fly in, arrivals snap into the swaying formation, the freed captive is invisible on its way down, and the challenging stage is fatally broken, since destroying a single enemy stops its wave counter and the game soft-locks on an empty screen at stage 3. A player gets two good Galaga stages and then a dead end.
